findings.title: Group view permission incorrectly grants manage/create access
findings.body: `canManage()` returns true when the caller has either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` on the all-groups resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`). `requireManage()` is used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` before creating a top-level group, so a principal granted only view access to all groups can create groups. It should require only `MANAGE`.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource ID instead of group ID
findings.body: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission(...)`, but `hasPermission` starts with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` the resource name is the actual group ID, while `groupResource.getId()` is the internal authorization resource UUID. It also adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. User search puts those IDs into `UserModel.GROUPS`, so the membership filter is wrong and can return no users for group view-members/manage-members permissions. It should use `groupResource.getName()` and add `groupResource.getName()`.

findings.title: Individually created group resources are not assigned the Groups type
findings.body: When `getOrCreateResource` creates a new resource for a group, it calls `resourceStore.create(...)` and updates scopes but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` discovers group resources with `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`, so these individual group resources will not be found; only the aggregate all-groups resource created in `init` has the type. This breaks group-membership-based user search filtering.

findings.title: Per-group authorization evaluation replaced one global short-circuit
findings.body: The new code filters with `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` instead of evaluating `groupsEvaluator.canView()` once and short-circuiting. For callers with fine-grained all-groups view/manage but no legacy admin role, `canView(group)` performs a resource lookup and policy evaluation for every group. On realms with many groups this makes the group listing endpoint significantly more expensive. The same pattern was removed in `GroupResource.getSubGroups`.
